item.text:
**4B.9 — Andrés Manuel López Obrador (2024)**  
**Bottom line:** negative. I found strong evidence of state-linked surveillance and online intimidation, plus obstruction of transparency/data-governance institutions. The positive side is limited to general cybersecurity / privacy-protection measures, which look defensive rather than politically repressive.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| + | [GUÍAS DE CIBERSEGURIDAD](https://www.gob.mx/gncertmx/acciones-y-programas/guias-de-ciberseguridad) | Guardia Nacional CERT-MX | 2024-04-25 | The government published cyber-hygiene guidance for firms and families, framed as resilience and private-data protection rather than political control. | 4B.9 |
| + | [La SSPC alerta a la ciudadanía sobre ataques cibernéticos en sistemas operativos para equipos de cómputo](https://www.gob.mx/sspc/prensa/la-sspc-alerta-a-la-ciudadania-sobre-ataques-ciberneticos-en-sistemas-operativos-para-equipos-de-computo) | SSPC | 2024-12-23 | SSPC issued a public warning about a zero-day vulnerability and remote device control, presenting the state as protecting users’ privacy and devices. | 4B.9 |
| - | [Mexico: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/mexico/freedom-net/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Freedom House said a covert SEDENA cyberspace unit monitored critics of the military or federal government, used inauthentic accounts, and tried to influence public opinion, while the government expanded surveillance with little oversight. | 4B.9, 4B.5, 4B.6 |
| - | [Mexico | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/mexico) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | AMLO publicly displayed a New York Times reporter’s personal information and phone number on broadcast, and YouTube removed the video under anti-harassment rules. | 4B.9, 4B.5, 4B.6 |
| - | [World Report 2024: Mexico](https://www.hrw.org/es/world-report/2024/country-chapters/mexico) | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | HRW said AMLO and his party blocked appointments to INAI, leaving the transparency/data-protection body unable to function normally and weakening access to information oversight. | 4B.9, 4B.4, 4B.6 |

**Search gap:** I did not find direct 2024 evidence of a nationwide internet shutdown or a formal presidential order to shut off access. The strongest evidence is instead about surveillance, online manipulation, doxxing/harassment, and blocking transparency institutions.
